title: kv-cache: improve eviction, defrag and spillover heuristics to reduce fragmentation and paging
author: Ethan Cole
description: Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and frequent paging to host memory under mixed workload patterns were increasing tail latency and GPU memory churn. This PR introduces a set of coordinated changes to eviction, defragmentation, and spillover heuristics to reduce fragmentation, defer paging, and prioritize hot prefixes. High level summary of changes: 1) Introduce a two-tier eviction score combining recency, frequency, and fragment-size penalty so highly fragmented small entries are deprioritized for long-lived residency; 2) Add background defragmentation pass that opportunistically coalesces adjacent free/partial segments when GPU utilization is low; 3) Implement spillover batching to aggregate multiple small spill candidates into single host-page transfers to reduce PCIe overhead; 4) Expose two runtime knobs (kv.defrag.enabled, kv.spill.batch_ms) and a fallback policy (prefer-compact/ prefer-recency). Approach: keep changes opt-in behind config defaults and the same observable surface (no protocol change). Eviction score: score = alpha*LRU_rank + beta*frequency_rank + gamma*fragment_penalty where fragment_penalty scales with the number of fragments contributed by the key. Defrag: background worker uses a rate-limited, low-priority allocator to merge adjacent free slots and relocate short-lived values when GPU load < 30% for > 5s. Spillover batching: small pages (< 64KB of real data) are grouped up to 512KB or up to batch_ms timeout and pushed in a single host transfer. Benchmarks: synthetic perf lab (gpt-like long-context mix) shows 18-24% reduction in paging IO, 10-15% decrease in 99th percentile latency for sequence lengths > 2048, and peak GPU memory reclaimed by defrag up to 6% on high-fragmentation workloads. Safety and rollout: feature gated and disabled by default for Dedicated customers; gradual rollout: canary on 5% of requests, then 25% after 48h, full rollout after automated metric validation. Tests: unit tests for scoring, integration test harness for background defrag, and perf canary run attached. Backwards compatibility: no wire changes; config flags can be toggled per-pool. Related work: builds on ENG-4221 (kv eviction v1) and ENG-4287 (spillover telemetry).

review_comments: Priya Nair (review): LGTM overall, please add a comment describing why fragment_penalty is proportional to fragment_count rather than fragment_size; that will help future tuning.

Author (Ethan): Added explanation and a short helper comment in cache_manager.cc; fragment_count was chosen because fragmentation tends to correlate with allocation churn rather than absolute bytes for our workloads.

Marco Li (review): Can we avoid doing heavy copies in defrag when GPU memory is under transient pressure? Suggest a hard cap per-defrag-op and better accounting so we don't conflict with serving tasks.
Author: Defrag now checks the allocator's available budget and limits relocation size to defrag.max_reloc_bytes; updated tests to assert behavior under constrained budgets.
Jules Benton (review): CI failed on macOS build due to missing include; also call out where the new runtime flags are surfaced in the console/API docs.
Author: Fixed include and added a short docs blurb + console feature flag mapping in serving/kv/config.yaml. All CI green after rerun. Approved by Priya and Marco.
Priya Nair (approval): approved+1, perf numbers look convincing on canary cluster
release_notes: Runtime: improve KV cache eviction and spillover heuristics. Reduces fragmentation and host paging in mixed workloads; exposes kv.defrag.enabled and kv.spill.batch_ms runtime knobs. Can be toggled per pool. (Non-breaking)
